name: Manufacturing
summary: The Ministry of Industry reports that manufacturing export earnings reached 607 million USD in the 2018 Ethiopian fiscal year (2025/26), and it targets 1 billion USD in the year that follows. The government reports industrial capacity utilization of 69.2 percent and about 5.9 billion USD in import substitution over the past fiscal year. Ethiopia remains ineligible for US AGOA trade preferences, though, and the World Bank says firms in industrial parks import more than 95 percent of their inputs.

opportunities.title: Integrated textile value chain
opportunities.detail: EIC promotes investment across cotton cultivation, ginning, spinning, weaving, dyeing and garment production, plus trims and accessories, in plug-and-play textile parks. Its page still cites AGOA access, which is out of date (see risks).

opportunities.title: Leather and leather products
opportunities.detail: EIC cites capacity of over 500 million square feet of finished leather a year, over USD 120 million a year from leather products, and specialized leather parks with zero-liquid-discharge treatment facilities.

opportunities.title: IPDC industrial parks and SEZs
opportunities.detail: IPDC offers serviced land and pre-built factory sheds with one-stop-shop services across 13 sites, including Bole Lemi, Hawassa, Kombolcha, Adama, Dire Dawa and Debre Birhan.

opportunities.title: Import substitution
opportunities.detail: The Ministry of Industry pairs the Made in Ethiopia initiative with an import substitution program and reports about 5.9 billion USD in import substitution within a single year.

opportunities.title: Pharmaceuticals (brief)
opportunities.detail: EIC cites an 85 percent import share in pharmaceutical supply and the 279-hectare Kilinto Industrial Park for pharmaceutical manufacturing; these figures come from a 2019 study.

incentives.detail: Up to 10 years income-tax holiday for enterprises producing inside industrial parks, and up to 15 years for industrial park developers.

Exemption from duties and other taxes on imports of machinery, equipment and construction material (also spare parts, raw materials and vehicles), a duty-free privilege for exporters, and bonded-export-factory schemes.
The Ethiopian Pharmaceutical Supply Agency gives local manufacturers 25 percent price protection against foreign suppliers and 30 percent advance payment under long-term agreements.
EIC cites preferential trade access under Everything But Arms, the African Continental Free Trade Area and COMESA for Ethiopia-based investors.

risks.detail: Ethiopia's AGOA eligibility was terminated in 2022 on human rights grounds, and Ethiopia is listed as ineligible for calendar year 2026.
AGOA itself is authorized only through December 31, 2026 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, P.L. 119-75), so extending it beyond that date would require new legislation.

The World Bank says manufacturing employment has been declining since 2018, partly influenced by the AGOA delisting, with job losses in apparel and textiles. Firms in industrial parks import more than 95 percent of their inputs.

The World Bank says liquidity shortages and lending caps restrict exporters' ability to fulfill international orders and expand operations, and smaller exporters are being excluded from bank financing.
Manufacturing's share of commercial banks' outstanding loans fell from 23 to 16.2 percent between June 2024 and June 2025.
